name: Altar of Storms (Burning Steppes)
summary: Blackrock warlocks perform fel rites at the Altar of Storms in the Burning Steppes. The dark monument draws those seeking demonic power.

sections.title: A Legacy of Shadow and Flame
sections.body: Blackrock warlocks hold the Altar of Storms, where they perform rites to channel fel magic and seal dark pacts. The monument was built during the earlier wars. Nearby, the hermit Gorzeeki Wildeyes and his master, Mor'zul Bloodbringer, keep an encampment overlooking the altar. Renegade practitioners study its violent energies and devise demanding rites for spellcasters who seek greater dark power.

faq.q: What is the Altar of Storms?
faq.answer: The Altar of Storms is a corrupted stone monument used for fel rites and to channel demonic energy. Built during the Old Horde's wars, it remains a source of dark power for Blackrock warlocks.

faq.q: Who controls the altar right now?
aliases: who is at altar of storms
faq.answer: Hostile Blackrock orc warlocks and acolytes occupy the grounds around the altar. They perform dark ceremonies and guard the site from intruders.

Gorzeeki Wildeyes is an eccentric goblin scholar of the dark arts and a hermit on the hill overlooking the altar. He lives there with his master, Mor'zul Bloodbringer, and helps powerful warlocks master greater demonic bindings.

angles.text: As a warlock, you can seek the materials and rites for summoning a dreaded dreadsteed from Mor'zul Bloodbringer and Gorzeeki Wildeyes, the hermits near the Altar of Storms.
As an orc, you may find the altar an uncomfortable reminder of the Old Horde's dark history. Gul'dan's Shadow Council used similar foul shrines to infuse ogres and soldiers with dark sorcery.
